title: Pool Surge Inspector + Autoscale Intent Editor - compact console controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact operations panel for Dedicated GPU pools that lets platform and SRE users inspect short-term surge behavior, author 'autoscale intent' policies, and apply burst overrides. This ticket covers UX flows, microcopy, telemetry hooks, and an accessibility pass for the compact inspector widget that will live in the pool list and the expanded pool detail sheet. Goals: (1) make burst overrides discoverable without disrupting default autoscale policies, (2) provide clear health signals and rollback affordances for rapid triage, and (3) expose intent configuration as a human-friendly policy (templates + freeform JSON for power users). Deliverables: Figma prototype (compact + expanded), annotated interaction spec, sample telemetry events, copy for confirmation/rollback modals, and a short usability script for internal QA.
comments: 2026-01-27 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: confirmed target personas (SRE on-call, infra PM, pool owner). Decided compact inspector should default to a passive mode (no auto-apply) and require explicit 'Activate Burst' confirmation.

2026-02-02 - Marcus Nguyen: First pass prototype uploaded to Figma. Includes three presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive), a freeform slider for burst duration (15m, 1h, 4h), and a cost-estimate preview tied to token throughput. Needs clearer error states for overlapping manual overrides.

2026-02-11 - Leah Brooks (PM): Reviewed microcopy; suggested changing 'Apply Burst' to 'Start Surge' to align with product glossary. Also requested an extra telemetry flag for 'manual_override_source' to differentiate CLI vs Console.

2026-02-18 - Diego Martinez (Eng - Runtime): Concern: 'Aggressive' preset maps to a kernel-level scheduling change that triggers a warm-up path. Recommended adding a 60s safety cooldown and presenting expected latency variance in the preview panel.
2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Updated prototype with cooldown, latency variance tooltip, and rollback button that queues an audited reversal. Added ARIA labels for toggle and slider controls.

2026-03-03 - Design review: Feedback: (a) make health signal colors accessible at 3:1 contrast, (b) add a compact timeline sparkline that layers SLO breaches with recent rollout events, (c) include link to affected routes and cost center in the confirmation modal.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Nguyen: Usability testing with 6 internal SREs: median task completion 48s to apply a 1h burst; two participants expected an undo to be immediate — clarified that undo queues a rollback but logs are updated instantly. Recommendation: add 'preview rollback ETA' copy.
2026-03-09 - Security: Reviewed: no new data retention concerns. Confirmed audit events are covered by existing KMS/HSM logging. Security review not required for UI-only change.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Preparing final handoff: annotated Figma + interaction spec pushed; PR link in attachments; scheduling handoff workshop for 2026-03-12 with Eng and PM.
notes: UX trade-offs considered: inline vs modal for presets. Chosen: inline compact control with modal-level confirmation to reduce context switch while preventing accidental activation.
Observability hooks: emit events for 'intent_created', 'intent_activated', 'intent_rolled_back', and 'intent_preview_requested' with metadata: pool_id, user_id, source, preset_id, duration_minutes.
Rollout plan: ship behind feature flag 'ui.pool.surge_inspector.v1' and gate by entitlement for Dedicated tenants. Canary to 10% of hosts for 72h, monitor SLO and cost delta dashboard.
Accessibility: keyboard-first interactions, explicit focus states, and live region update when a rollback completes.
